THE ANCIENT COVENANT RECORD

Volume Forty-Seven

The Book of Mysteries

SEFER HA-RAZIM

The Book of Mysteries — Complete

All Fragments — 1Q27, 4Q299, 4Q300, 4Q301

The Mystery of Existence — The Wicked and the Righteous — Eschatological Wisdom

PRIMARY MANUSCRIPT AUTHORITIES

Primary: 1Q27 — Cave 1, Qumran — Hebrew — 1st century BCE

4Q299 — Cave 4, Qumran — Hebrew — Multiple fragments — Primary witness

4Q300 — Cave 4, Qumran — Hebrew — Parallel fragments

4Q301 — Cave 4, Qumran — Aramaic overlay — Minor witness

Qumran Sectarian Composition — No Masoretic parallel — No Orit Ge'ez parallel

Divine Names: YHWH and The Creator only — no substitutions

COMPARATIVE NOTES AT END OF EVERY CHAPTER

DSS · ORIT GE'EZ · MASORETIC VARIANT · CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitute titles

INTRODUCTION TO THE BOOK OF MYSTERIES

1 The Book of Mysteries — Sefer ha-Razim in Hebrew — is a Qumran sectarian wisdom composition attested across four manuscript witnesses: 1Q27 from Cave 1 and 4Q299, 4Q300, and 4Q301 from Cave 4. The text belongs to the broader category of Qumran's wisdom literature, sharing conceptual terrain with the Instruction text (4QInstruction) and the Community Rule, while advancing a distinctive theology of hidden divine knowledge reserved for the righteous community.

2 The central theme is the contrast between the wicked who do not perceive the mystery of existence and the righteous who have been granted access to the hidden counsel of YHWH. The Hebrew term raz nihyeh — the mystery of existence or the mystery of that which is — appears as the cornerstone concept, denoting the divine plan embedded in creation that only the illuminated can discern.

3 The manuscript evidence is fragmentary. 4Q299 preserves the most substantial remains, running to multiple columns with partial text. 1Q27 provides the earliest witnessed copy. 4Q300 offers overlapping parallel passages. 4Q301 introduces Aramaic elements suggesting transmission across linguistic communities within the Qumran movement. The reconstruction presented here follows the scholarly composite established by Lawrence Schiffman and the DJD critical edition, prioritizing 4Q299 where witnesses overlap.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 1Q27 was among the original Cave 1 discoveries of 1947. The manuscript is written in a Herodian formal script, dating to the late 1st century BCE. 4Q299-301 from Cave 4 significantly expanded the known text when published in the Discoveries in the Judaean Desert series. 4Q299 is the longest witness with approximately 70 identified fragments.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Book of Mysteries has no direct parallel in the Orit Ge'ez corpus. The closest conceptual parallel is the wisdom tradition embedded in Chanokh, particularly the sections concerning the heavenly tablets and the secrets revealed to Chanokh on the mountain. The concept of hidden knowledge reserved for the elect community is consistent with the theological framework of Beta Israel sacred literature.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Book of Mysteries has no Masoretic canon equivalent. It is a sectarian composition entirely absent from the Hebrew Bible as transmitted by the Rabbis. This absence reinforces the scholarly consensus that the Masoretic canon reflects selective transmission that excluded Qumran community literature from the received text.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The raz nihyeh formula — the mystery of existence — is unique to Qumran literature and represents one of the most significant theological concepts in the entire DSS corpus. Its absence from later canonical compilations strongly suggests deliberate exclusion rather than unknown authorship. The concept establishes that divine wisdom extends beyond Torah alone.

PART ONE — THE MYSTERY OF EXISTENCE — 1Q27 AND 4Q299

FRAGMENT 1 — THE MYSTERY OF EXISTENCE — 1Q27 Column 1 and 4Q299 Fragments 1-3

1 [The mystery of existence — raz nihyeh — and all its manifestations]: consider them and know what will come upon them, what is appointed and what will be. And do not pursue evil, for the wicked will perish.

2 YHWH knows every secret counsel of the nations, and He does not close His eyes upon any iniquity. The deeds of wickedness are in His sight continually, and the children of injustice cannot hide from His gaze.

3 Those who walk in the stubbornness of their hearts have not perceived the mystery of existence, nor have they understood the ancient matters. They have not known what will come upon them, and they have not saved themselves from the mystery of existence.

4 This shall be the sign for you that these things shall come to pass: when the begotten of injustice are delivered up, and wickedness is removed from before righteousness as darkness is removed from before light.

5 As smoke disappears and is no more, so shall wickedness disappear forever, and righteousness shall be revealed as the sun throughout all the appointed times of eternity. And all who hold fast to the mysteries of wonder shall be no more.

6 Then you shall know the truth, and the iniquity shall vanish like smoke, and the mystery of existence shall be revealed to all who seek it in purity of heart and cleanness of hands.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 1Q27 Column 1 is the foundational witness to this passage. The phrase raz nihyeh appears at least three times in this column, establishing it as the thematic signature of the entire composition. The DSS editors John Allegro and subsequently Lawrence Schiffman date the composition itself to the 2nd century BCE though the manuscripts are later copies.

[ORIT GE'EZ] No direct Orit Ge'ez parallel. The concept of hidden divine knowledge revealed to the righteous parallels the Chanokh tradition of heavenly secrets disclosed on the sacred mountain. The removal of wickedness like smoke before light echoes eschatological imagery present in the Ethiopic Chanokh corpus, suggesting shared ancient Afro-Asiatic wisdom traditions predating the sectarian Qumran community.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No Masoretic parallel. The Masoretic wisdom tradition, represented by Mishlei and Kohelet, addresses the contrast between the wise and the foolish but does not employ the raz nihyeh formula or the specific eschatological framework of hidden mysteries reserved for an elect community. This is a distinctively Qumran theological formulation.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The phrase "begotten of injustice" is a technical Qumran designation for those outside the covenant community. The eschatological framework — wickedness removed as darkness before light — reflects a dualistic worldview consistent with the Community Rule and the War Scroll. The mystery of existence functions not as abstract philosophy but as the specific divine plan governing history, accessible only to the covenant community through study of the sacred texts.

FRAGMENT 2 — THE HIDDEN COUNSEL — 4Q299 Fragments 4-8

1 [The knowledge of good and evil] has been given to the children of light, that they may discern between the holy and the profane, and that they may know the mystery that is coming upon the world. For YHWH has appointed times for all things, and to each generation its portion.

2 Has not YHWH established the boundary of the nations? And has He not appointed the times of their rise and their fall? All is written in the book of remembrance before Him, and nothing escapes His counsel.

3 The children of wickedness say in their hearts: The Creator does not see, and the knowledge of the Most High is far from us. But they shall know when the appointed time arrives that their counsel was vanity, and their deeds will testify against them.

4 Seek the mystery of existence in every age and in every generation. Meditate upon it day and night. For in it is the knowledge of all times from the beginning until the end, and the hidden things of the ages are made plain to those who seek diligently.

5 The wicked shall seek the mystery but will not find it, because they have not walked in the paths of righteousness and have not cleansed their hearts before YHWH. The mystery is sealed to the unclean, but open as a gate of light to those who fear The Creator.

6 [Write therefore these things upon the tablets of your heart,] and inscribe them upon the doorposts of your understanding, that the mystery of existence may be your guide in every way and your lamp in every darkness.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q299 Fragments 4-8 preserve this material with gaps indicated by brackets. The reference to writing upon tablets of the heart echoes Yirmeyahu 31:33 and represents a Qumran interpretation of the new covenant tradition applied to wisdom instruction rather than Torah law. The DSS editor Devorah Dimant has identified this passage as central to understanding the Qumran community's self-conception as the recipients of hidden divine wisdom.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The concept of appointed times for nations directly parallels the Orit Ge'ez Yovelim framework in which YHWH appoints the jubilee calendar governing all human history. The "book of remembrance" parallels the heavenly tablets tradition prominent throughout the Orit Ge'ez canon. These convergences suggest a shared ancient Afro-Asiatic theological vocabulary predating the Qumran sectarian context.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The phrase "appointed times" (Hebrew: mo'adim) appears throughout the Masoretic text but without the eschatological specificity of the Qumran usage. The Masoretic tradition interprets mo'adim primarily as liturgical festivals rather than the cosmological time-structure implied in the Qumran wisdom texts. This represents a significant divergence in theological interpretation.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The contrast between the wicked who seek the mystery and cannot find it versus the righteous to whom it is revealed establishes an epistemological barrier rooted in moral status rather than intellectual capacity. This is a radical theological claim: truth is not accessible through reason alone but requires covenant faithfulness. This concept is entirely absent from Greek philosophical tradition and represents a distinctively ancient Semitic theological framework.

PART TWO — WISDOM AND WICKEDNESS — 4Q299 AND 4Q300

FRAGMENT 3 — THE DECEPTION OF THE WICKED — 4Q299 Fragments 9-15

1 [The wicked] have exchanged the glory of YHWH for the vanity of their own counsels. They have taught smooth things and interpreted falsehood. They have prophesied to the people lies and led them from the paths of righteousness into the ways of destruction.

2 Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity and sin as with a cart rope. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter.

3 These have no portion in the mystery of existence. Their wisdom is the wisdom of the flesh and their counsel is the counsel of vanity. They shall be swept away when the spirit of judgment passes through the land as a consuming fire.

4 But the righteous, who walk in the light of the mystery, shall stand firm in the day of judgment. Their foundation is laid upon the rock of truth, and the waters of wickedness shall not overwhelm them.

5 For YHWH has chosen them from among the nations and set them apart for Himself from the beginning of creation. Their names are written in the book of the living, and their deeds are remembered before the throne of glory.

6 Therefore study the mystery of existence with all your heart and with all your understanding. Turn from evil and do good. Seek peace and pursue it. And the knowledge of YHWH shall be your inheritance forever.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q299 Fragments 9-15 are among the better-preserved sections of the Cave 4 manuscripts. The phrase "smooth things" is a technical Qumran designation appearing also in the Pesher Nahum (4QpNah) and refers to those who interpret Torah leniently — generally identified with the Pharisaic movement. This confirms the sectarian polemical dimension of the wisdom text alongside its theological content.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The "book of the living" — a heavenly register of the righteous — has strong parallels in the Chanokh corpus (Chanokh 47:3, 81:1-3) where the heavenly tablets record the deeds of all human beings. The Orit Ge'ez tradition preserves this concept with greater detail than the fragmentary Qumran text, suggesting the heavenly tablets theology preceded and informed the Qumran sectarian appropriation.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The "woe" oracles in this passage closely parallel the language of Yeshayahu 5:20, which the Masoretic tradition preserves. This suggests the Book of Mysteries author drew on prophetic literature that was subsequently incorporated into the Masoretic canon, using it within a wisdom framework. The DSS version may preserve a more original form of this prophetic material than the later Masoretic compilation.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The reference to those who "taught smooth things and interpreted falsehood" alongside the contrast of mystery-possessors versus the excluded wicked has led scholars including Geza Vermes and John Collins to identify the Book of Mysteries as evidence of intense inner-Israelite sectarian conflict during the Second Temple period. The text encodes a community under existential threat from rival interpretive authorities, using the framework of hidden wisdom to assert exclusive legitimacy.

FRAGMENT 4 — THE NATURE OF THE MYSTERY — 4Q300 Fragments 1-6

1 [What is the mystery of existence?] It is the hidden counsel of YHWH concerning all that He created from the beginning: the heavens and the earth, the deep and the waters, light and darkness, the appointed times of the sun and the courses of the moon.

2 It is the knowledge of all the ages that are to come, and the understanding of the deeds of the children of flesh in every generation, and the accounting that will be required of every living soul at the end of days.

3 YHWH inscribed it upon the heavenly tablets before the creation of the world, that those who seek wisdom might find it written in the pattern of all that exists. For creation itself is the visible form of the mystery, and the one who understands creation understands the mystery.

4 Study the alternation of day and night. Study the courses of the stars and the seasons of the year. In these you will find the mystery written plainly. For YHWH has encoded His counsel in the structure of what He made, and the righteous mind can read it.

5 But the unrighteous look upon creation and see only matter. They do not perceive the pattern beneath the visible things. Therefore they stumble in darkness even in the light of day, and they shall not know what comes upon them until it overtakes them.

6 To the one who has been given understanding: guard the mystery. Speak of it only among those who have ears to hear. Do not cast the sacred knowledge before those who will trample it, for the mystery is the most precious of all treasures and must be guarded with the whole life.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q300 Fragments 1-6 parallel and supplement 4Q299 at several points, allowing partial reconstruction of lacunae. The description of the mystery as encoded in the structure of creation connects the Book of Mysteries to the broader Qumran cosmological tradition seen in the Songs of Sabbath Sacrifice and the astronomical sections of Chanokh. The 364-day solar calendar that governs Qumran practice is itself understood as part of the mystery of creation's structure.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez tradition in Chanokh chapters 72-82 provides detailed astronomical wisdom concerning the courses of the sun and moon. The connection between creation's pattern and divine wisdom in this fragment directly parallels the Ge'ez astronomical book, suggesting both texts draw on a common Afro-Asiatic cosmological wisdom tradition. In the Ge'ez tradition this knowledge was revealed to Chanokh personally by the angel Uriel.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic wisdom tradition in Mishlei 8 personifies wisdom as present at creation, but does not develop the concept of a hidden mystery encoded in creation's structure that must be guarded and transmitted only to the worthy. The Qumran framework represents a significant development beyond anything preserved in the Masoretic wisdom corpus, suggesting substantial theological development that the Masoretic canonization process did not preserve.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The injunction to guard the mystery and speak it only among the worthy is consistent with the Community Rule's regulations governing the staged disclosure of community teaching to initiates over a three-year period. The Book of Mysteries therefore functions not as speculative theology but as a community formation text: it describes the knowledge that the community possesses and that marks them as distinct from all outside groups. This is the epistemological foundation of Qumran sectarian identity.

PART THREE — ESCHATOLOGICAL JUDGMENT — 4Q299 COLUMN FRAGMENTS

FRAGMENT 5 — THE END OF WICKEDNESS — 4Q299 Fragments 16-22

1 The appointed time is coming and it will not be delayed. YHWH has set a seal upon it in the mystery of existence, and when the seal is broken the age of wickedness will end and the age of righteousness will begin. No human counsel can prevent it.

2 In that day the children of darkness will seek a place to flee and will find none. The mountains will not hide them and the depths of the earth will not cover them. They will be brought out from their hiding places and made to stand before the judgment.

3 All the deeds of the wicked are written and will be read aloud in the hearing of all creation. Every secret counsel of injustice will be made public. Every word spoken in darkness will be spoken in the light. Every hidden thing will be revealed.

4 But the righteous will stand in the assembly of the holy ones. Their deeds also will be read, and they will shine like the brightness of the firmament. YHWH will seat them in the place of honor and give them authority over those who oppressed them.

5 This is the guarantee of the mystery: that the moral structure of creation, though invisible to the wicked in the present age, will become fully visible in the age to come. Righteousness is not merely preferable — it is embedded in the fabric of existence, and it will prevail.

6 Therefore do not be troubled by the prosperity of the wicked in this age, nor discouraged by the suffering of the righteous. These are temporary. The mystery of existence guarantees the reversal. Hold fast to the covenant and the appointed time will vindicate you.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q299 Fragments 16-22 preserve this eschatological sequence with significant lacunae. The structural parallel to the Community Rule's Two Spirits Treatise (1QS 3-4) is unmistakable: both texts describe a cosmic dualism resolving at an eschatological visitation. John Collins in his analysis of Qumran apocalypticism identifies the Book of Mysteries as one of the earliest witnesses to this theological framework within the Qumran corpus.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The eschatological reversal described here — the righteous exalted, the wicked exposed and judged — has strong parallels in Chanokh 38:1-6 and 62:1-16 in the Orit Ge'ez tradition. The image of the righteous shining like the firmament appears in Daniyel 12:3 and is developed extensively in the Ge'ez Chanokh. This convergence across the DSS and Orit Ge'ez traditions points to a shared ancient Afro-Asiatic eschatological theology predating both compositions.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic tradition preserves limited eschatological material comparable to this passage. Daniyel 12 is the closest parallel within the canon. The absence of robust eschatological judgment theology in the Masoretic corpus, compared to its prominence in both the DSS and the Orit Ge'ez, supports the conclusion that the Masoretic canon reflects a theological selection that minimized eschatological speculation in favor of legal and liturgical material.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The pastoral function of this eschatological passage is crucial: it addresses the community's experience of social marginalization and persecution by reframing present suffering within a cosmic narrative of guaranteed vindication. This is not escapism but a sophisticated theological response to historical oppression. The Book of Mysteries therefore serves simultaneously as cosmological wisdom text, community formation document, and pastoral consolation literature.

FRAGMENT 6 — THE FINAL SUMMATION — 4Q301 AND CLOSING FRAGMENTS

1 [Thus speaks the one who knows the mystery:] I have looked upon all that YHWH has done from the beginning, and I have searched the pattern of the ages, and this is what I have found: righteousness is the foundation of all creation, and YHWH will not abandon it.

2 The wicked imagine that the absence of immediate judgment means the absence of any judge. They are deceived by the patience of The Creator. His patience is not weakness. His delay is not abandonment. His silence in this age is the silence before the storm of judgment.

3 But to those who have received the mystery of existence, the silence of YHWH is not silence at all. It is the sound of creation moving toward its appointed culmination, inexorable as the rising of the sun, unstoppable as the turning of the seasons.

4 Guard therefore the mystery among you. Teach it to your children and to all who are worthy to receive it. Let it be the framework within which you interpret everything that happens, for without it the events of history are random and cruel, but within it they are the working out of the counsel of YHWH.

5 And in the last of the days, when the mystery is fully revealed and the age of righteousness is established, YHWH will be known not by a few but by all who remain. The knowledge of The Creator will cover the earth as the waters cover the sea.

6 This is the end of the mystery of existence. He who has ears, let him hear. He who has eyes, let him see. He who has understanding, let him understand. And let the one who has been given all three praise YHWH with his whole heart, for he has been given the greatest gift that can be given to a living soul.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q301 provides Aramaic parallels to the closing material, with sufficient overlap to confirm the Hebrew text. The bilingual transmission suggests the Book of Mysteries circulated across both Hebrew-speaking and Aramaic-speaking communities within the broader Qumran movement. The closing formula "he who has ears let him hear" appears in this form only in the DSS; the later appearance of similar language in other traditions represents independent development from this shared ancient source.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The final vision of universal divine knowledge covering the earth as waters cover the sea directly quotes the language of Yeshayahu 11:9 in its Ge'ez form as preserved in the Orit canon. The Ge'ez tradition preserves this verse in a fuller form than the Masoretic, and the Book of Mysteries' use of it suggests the author knew a version of Yeshayahu's text closer to the Ge'ez tradition than the later Masoretic standardization. This is significant evidence for the priority of the Afro-Asiatic textual tradition.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic text of Yeshayahu 11:9 preserves the "knowledge covering the earth as waters" image, but the Masoretic tradition does not connect it to the raz nihyeh concept of hidden wisdom. The Book of Mysteries represents the missing link between prophetic eschatology and wisdom theology — a theological synthesis that the Masoretic canonization process did not preserve in any single text, though traces appear scattered across multiple books.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The closing of the Book of Mysteries is among the most remarkable passages in the entire DSS corpus. The invitation to the one who possesses hearing, sight, and understanding simultaneously — and who should therefore praise YHWH — implies a small and exclusive audience. The text ends not with commandment but with doxology, suggesting that the ultimate purpose of all wisdom is not knowledge for its own sake but the praise of The Creator. This theological conclusion places the Book of Mysteries within the same devotional framework as the Hodayot (Thanksgiving Psalms) and represents a coherent Qumran theology of wisdom, covenant, and worship.
